payload.name: Loss aversion in noninstrumental information
payload.fact: Loss aversion, the endowment effect, and the gain-loss framing effect apply to noninstrumental information in a manner analogous to their application to material goods.

provenance.title: Loss aversion, the endowment effect, and gain-loss framing shape preferences for noninstrumental information
provenance.quote_or_locus: we show that three key phenomena which characterize the valuation of money and material goods—loss aversion, the endowment effect, and the gain-loss framing effect—also apply to noninstrumental information
